content.value: Combine conditions with &&, ||, and !; use short-circuit evaluation to guard unsafe expressions; express ranges correctly.

Logical AND (&&) requires both operands, OR (||) accepts either or both, and NOT (!) negates one boolean value. Negation binds most tightly, then AND, then OR; parentheses make the intended grouping explicit. A range usually needs two comparisons joined with AND, rather than a chained numeric comparison.

Evaluation proceeds left to right and can short-circuit. If the left side of && is false, the right side is skipped. If the left side of || is true, the right side is skipped. Put safety checks before operations that require them, such as a nonzero check before division or a non-null check before an instance call.

Both results are false. The first left operand rejects null, so length() is not called. The second rejects zero, so division is skipped. Reversing either pair would evaluate the unsafe operation first.

OR is inclusive: both conditions may be true. x >= 1 || x <= 5 is true for every ordinary integer and is not a bounded-range test. Avoid relying on omitted right-side effects; make important updates explicit.
Write a safe condition that checks whether a non-null String s contains at least three characters. Answer: s != null && s.length() >= 3. Test null, an empty String, and a three-character String.
